newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.08 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.08 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended early gains on Thursday afternoon with the help of liquidity inflow and rising hopes that a newly formed right-left coalition will win a confidence vote on July 12, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,912, up 39 points or 2.08 percent from Wednesday's previous record of 1,873. But it was down slightly from a late trading record of 1,916.
Volume rose to 27.48 trillion lira from Wednesday's 24.41 trillion.
"The market continues to rise quietly. It can test the 2,000 level with the help of a second buying wave in blue chip state and energy shares," said Gokhan Ozdemir from Alan Securities.
"But I'd advise investors to keep away from stocks which have posted strong premiums. It would be logical to turn to cheaper issues," he added.

Brokers said the market would aim for the 2,000 level with selective activity until the July 12 confidence vote in parliament, with six-month profit prospects of companies expected to influence purchases.
They said the market was likely to concentrate on economic fundamentals after the vote.

Conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz's alliance which was approved by the President on Monday, is a minority coalition of two right and one left-wing parties, supported by another left-wing party.

Yilmaz has predicted that his government would win the vote with a bigger-than-expected margin after the recent defections from the alliance of former Prime Minister and Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan and his conservative ally Tansu Ciller.

Of the 248 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 182 to 25 and 41 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial gained 2.11 percent to 1,790, the IMKB Services firmed 0.87 percent to 1,864 and the IMKB Financial jumped 2.24 percent to 2,099.

Actives were led by largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, up 4,000 lira at 88,000, flat steel maker Eregli, up 250 lira at 24,750, T.Isbank's C series, up 2,000 lira to 62,000 and newly listed textile firm EGS Egeser which closed at 12,500.
They made up 17.2 percent of the total turnover.

The Exchange listed partial shares of two new firms -- EGS Egeser Giyim Sanayi Ic ve Dis Ticaret AS and frozen food producer Apeks Dis Ticaret AS -- on the national market today. The opening prices were 11,500 lira for Egeser and 11,000 lira for Apeks which ended at 11,750 lira.
